newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian dollar deposits little changed in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits little changed in late trade.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were little changed in lacklustre trade on Friday, dealers said.

They said most traders were sidelined ahead of tonight's release of the U.S. second quarter final gross domestic product (GDP) figures and the University of Michigan final sentiment index for September.

The reading for the second quarter for the GDP figures is forecast to show a growth of 4.6 pecent compared with a reading of 4.8 percent reported in the previous report. The September University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment Index is expected to be around 95.1 percent against August's 95.3 percent.

"The market was quiet and featureless in the morning on some position adjustments. Some people are waiting for tonight's second quarter GDP and University of Michigan consumer sentiment index figures for more clues to market direction, but unless the numbers are way off market expectations, I don't think there will be much impact," a local dealer said.
In day-to-day rates, weekend and Monday/Tuesday slipped 1/8 percentage point each to a common 5-1/4 5-1/8 percent, respectively.

Among longer dates, two-months was unchanged from Thursday's 5-1/2 5-3/8 percent, four-months unchanged at 5-9/16 5-7/16, six-months unchanged at 5-3/4 5-5/8 and twelve-months unchanged at 6 5-7/8 percent. -- P. Theseira (65-870-3085)
